methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Compute fleet run-off at spot by vintage $448B (cash flows [55744, 95360, 69755, 127236, 89796, 78438, 51211, 29130, 18163, 0] at 9.19%, no TV); Starlink subscriber DCF $196B; Space Starship tree $59.5B; Starlink knock-on -$9.3B; X $8B; Cursor $60B equity; 10% holdco discount; net debt $69B; EchoStar cash -$7.7B and Tesla -$15B expected

inputs_detail.derivation: Relative to a new chip at the same date: in today's shortage, marketplace H100 ~$2.8/hr (Silicon Data $2.81 on 2026-10-07) over ~1.3 kW all-in = ~$19/W-yr vs B300 median ~$6.2/hr over ~1.9 kW = ~$29/W-yr, a ratio of ~0.66 at ~3 years; CoreWeave list prices per watt are flatter still (H100 $6.16 vs B200 $8.60 per GPU-hr). In normal times the KrASIA industry rule is ~80% decline over five years (0.725^age), and the 2023-24 cycle took H100 from >$4.70 (2023) to ~$2.85 (early 2024) and $1-2 auctions by Aug 2024 (Latent Space). 0.785^age (0.48 at 3y, 0.30 at 5y) sits between the normal-times rule and the shortage reading.

NPV 0 at 9.19% of a vintage earning P x 0.785^age x 90% less $4/W-yr opex, 21% tax on EBIT after 6-year SL depreciation, 15% salvage (script model.py breakeven()). Path sits ~2x above it through 2028, so the 2029-30 build window (3 GW a year at $32/$31 per W) is valued; builds after 2030 earn break-even (NPV 0).

reverse_dcf_check: 15x NTM EBITDA on ~$106B, with D&A/capex near half of EBITDA, is ~30x unlevered FCF, which at 9.19% implies ~6%/yr perpetual FCF growth at today's margins; our run-off says fleet margins fall as $/W-yr fades toward ~$23, so the 15x leg (and today's $1.9T EV) is only consistent with the shortage lasting past 2030 or with large value outside our parts.

reasoning: Base-rates lane. (1) Facts: Q3 revenue $14.6B (+161%), SI $7.6B, 1.7 GW nameplate (2.2 GW end-Oct), Q4 capex guide $35-40B (~2x the August guide), net cash $51B, 12.9B economic diluted shares -> $1.95T market cap. (2) 8 vs 13 GW: the near-term guide beat, but stretch targets from Musk companies have a poor on-time record (Verdict); holding today's ~0.4 GW/month gives 8 GW, which matches S&P Global's $197B 2027 SpaceX capex; 13 GW needs ~$350B and ~20 GW of power Musk calls difficult. Weighted ~8.3 GW. (3) Shortage durability: indices are rising now (SemiAnalysis H100 1-yr +38%, Ornn +22% in a month, Nebius/AWS hikes), but the 2023-24 cycle shows rents halving within ~10 months once supply lands, and 2027 industry capex is ~$1.3T. I hold $48 in 2027 and fade to break-even (~$23, computed) by 2031. (4) Valuation per Kilian's legs gives $79.58 (EV/EBITDA $115, SOTP $45, P/E $78); scenario recomputes $25 / $80 / $180. (5) Price forecast: the stock trades ~1.9x our value; valuation gaps close slowly, mega-IPOs drift negative in year one, and lock-up supply runs to March 2027, so the base price is $122 (premium closes ~35%), bear $55, bull $230 at 0.25/0.5/0.25 with 28-32% within-scenario vol: median ~$122, P(>= today) ~0.34. model_inputs.structure_note: Kilian's legs: 0.4 consolidated EV/EBITDA 15x NTM (GAAP, after SBC), 0.4 SOTP, 0.2 P/E 27x; no DCF leg (SPCX is not a neocloud). The segment_build carries SI (external share of fleet spot value + Grok/Cursor/X), Connectivity (subs x ARPU + E&G) and Space. The SOTP carries the value of record: the compute fleet as a run-off by vintage at spot (cash_flows, no terminal value, 2029-30 build window), Starlink subscriber DCF with RONIC = WACC after 2035, Space as Starship scenarios, Starlink knock-on, X and Cursor at marks, 10% holdco discount, 9.19% on every cash-flow part. Net debt at the horizon is stated from a quarterly bridge (the engine's annual pro-rating would understate Q4-26's doubled capex). The consolidated legs treat internal-use watts as cost without GAAP revenue; the SOTP credits them at spot. Their gap (EV/EBITDA $115 vs SOTP $45) is mostly the multiple: 15x on NTM EBITDA earned at ~1.8x break-even pricing assumes it lasts; the run-off says it fades.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) I kept 15x EV/EBITDA and 27x P/E; base-rate evidence on peak-cycle pricing argues for ~12x, which would cut FV by ~$9. (2) I exclude 1,302M restricted Musk Class B shares (Mars-colony / 100 TW off-Earth compute conditions); counting them cuts every value ~9%. (3) Cursor acquisition SBC is excluded from EBIT because its awards are in the diluted count (counted once). (4) Engine scenario deltas cannot swap the price path inside cash-flow parts; full recomputes give bear $24.9 / bull $180.0 vs deltas $34.1 / $171.2. (5) Grok at NPV 0 is generous: SI non-compute costs (~$6-8B/yr fixed model R&D) are carried only in the consolidated legs.
